276	    // MARK: - Where the converted file goes
277	
278	    /// `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Rewrapped/`.
279	    ///
280	    /// **Why not inside the `.framejob` package**, which is what spec §11's
281	    /// one-line sketch says. Two reasons, both discovered in the code:
282	    ///
283	    /// 1. There is frequently no package. Opening an MKV from the Finder
284	    ///    builds an UNTITLED document (`ProjectDocument.readMediaFile` nils
285	    ///    `fileURL` deliberately, and `intendedCacheDirectory` falls back to a
286	    ///    temporary directory precisely because of it). The import that needs
287	    ///    the conversion is the very import that has nowhere to put it, and a
288	    ///    file written to `NSTemporaryDirectory()` is orphaned by the first
289	    ///    Save As — which costs nothing for a regenerable thumbnail and loses
290	    ///    the user's footage here.
291	    /// 2. `ProjectDocument.fileWrapper(ofType:)` writes a package with
292	    ///    exactly two children, `project.json` and `cache`. Anything else put
293	    ///    in the bundle is dropped by the next save, autosave included. The
294	    ///    one surviving location, `cache/`, is documented as regenerable and
295	    ///    deletable (§5.6) — the last place to keep the only decodable copy of
296	    ///    somebody's source material.
297	    ///
298	    /// Application Support has neither problem: it exists before the document
299	    /// does, it survives every save and Save As, and a reopened project finds
300	    /// the file by the same absolute path it recorded. It is also shared, so
301	    /// importing the same MKV into a second project reuses the first
302	    /// conversion instead of paying for it twice. This keeps the §11 decision
303	    /// intact — media is *referenced*, not copied into the document — and the
304	    /// converted file behaves like any other referenced media: move it and the
305	    /// Media tab badges it missing and offers Relink…
306	    ///
307	    /// The two path components were spelled here, privately, until road map
308	    /// 2's phase 7 needed the same folder for `ExportPresets.json`. They are
309	    /// `AppSupport`'s now — one home for `~/Library/Application
310	    /// Support/Frame Job/`, which is where the argument above still lives; this
311	    /// only names the subfolder. The directory itself is still created by
312	    /// `convert`, at the moment there is something to put in it.
313	    static var rewrapDirectory: URL? {
314	        AppSupport.subdirectory("Rewrapped")
315	    }
316	
317	    /// The converted file's name for `source`: the source's own stem, so the
318	    /// Media tab still reads recognisably, plus a digest of the source's
319	    /// path, size and modification date. The digest is what makes the result
320	    /// reusable AND self-invalidating — re-importing the same file finds the
321	    /// existing conversion, while re-encoding the source under the same name
322	    /// produces a different digest and a fresh conversion rather than a stale
323	    /// one.
324	    static func destination(for source: URL) -> URL? {
325	        guard let directory = rewrapDirectory, let digest = digest(of: source) else { return nil }
326	        return directory.appendingPathComponent("\(stem(of: source))-\(digest).mov")
327	    }
328	
329	    /// A finished conversion of `source`, if one is already on disk. Checked
330	    /// before ffmpeg is even looked for, so a project whose media was
331	    /// converted last month still opens on a machine where ffmpeg has since
332	    /// been uninstalled.
333	    static func existingRewrap(of source: URL) -> URL? {
334	        guard let destination = destination(for: source),
335	            FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: destination.path)
336	        else { return nil }
337	        return destination
338	    }
339	
340	    /// Throws away a conversion that turned out to be unopenable, so the next
341	    /// import tries again instead of handing the same bad file back for ever
342	    /// — `existingRewrap` cannot tell a good `.mov` from a bad one, and only
343	    /// the caller that re-probed it knows.
344	    ///
345	    /// Refuses to delete anything that is not directly inside
346	    /// `rewrapDirectory`. This takes a URL and removes a file, which is
347	    /// exactly the shape of function that a bug elsewhere turns into a data
348	    /// loss, so the guard is not a formality.
349	    static func discard(_ url: URL) {
350	        guard let directory = rewrapDirectory,
351	            url.deletingLastPathComponent().standardizedFileURL.path
352	                == directory.standardizedFileURL.path
353	        else { return }
354	        try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: url)
355	    }
356	
357	    /// FNV-1a over path, byte size and modification second. Not a content
358	    /// hash: reading gigabytes to decide whether to convert gigabytes is the
359	    /// wrong trade, and the three attributes together already distinguish
360	    /// every file this will ever see. A collision would reuse the wrong
361	    /// conversion, which is why the *name* also carries the source's stem.
362	    private static func digest(of source: URL) -> String? {
363	        let attributes = try? FileManager.default.attributesOfItem(atPath: source.path)
364	        guard let size = (attributes?[.size] as? NSNumber)?.int64Value else { return nil }
365	        let modified = (attributes?[.modificationDate] as? Date)?.timeIntervalSince1970 ?? 0
366	        var hash: UInt64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325
367	        for byte in "\(source.path)|\(size)|\(Int64(modified.rounded()))".utf8 {
368	            hash = (hash ^ UInt64(byte)) &* 0x0000_0100_0000_01b3
369	        }
370	        let hex = String(hash, radix: 16)
371	        return String(repeating: "0", count: max(0, 16 - hex.count)) + hex
372	    }
373	
374	    /// The source's base name reduced to characters that are unambiguous in a
375	    /// file name. This string is built from a file name the app did not
376	    /// choose, and it becomes a path component — so it is filtered rather
377	    /// than trusted, and bounded so a pathological name cannot push the
378	    /// result past the file system's limit.
379	    private static func stem(of source: URL) -> String {
380	        let allowed = CharacterSet.alphanumerics.union(CharacterSet(charactersIn: "-_"))
381	        let characters = source.deletingPathExtension().lastPathComponent.unicodeScalars.map {
382	            allowed.contains($0) ? Character($0) : "_"
383	        }
384	        let text = String(characters.prefix(48))
385	        return text.isEmpty ? "media" : text
386	    }

388	    // MARK: - Consent
389	
390	    /// Puts the cost in front of the user and returns their answer. Safe from
391	    /// any thread; on a background thread it hops to main and waits, which is
392	    /// sound because `assist` deliberately holds no lock across this call —
393	    /// see the comment there.
394	    static func consent(for plan: Plan) -> Bool {
395	        if Thread.isMainThread { return ask(plan) }
396	        var accepted = false
397	        DispatchQueue.main.sync { accepted = ask(plan) }
398	        return accepted
399	    }
400	
401	    private static func ask(_ plan: Plan) -> Bool {
402	        let alert = NSAlert()
403	        alert.alertStyle = .informational
404	        alert.messageText = "Frame Job cannot open “\(plan.source.lastPathComponent)”."
405	        alert.informativeText = plan.consentText
406	        alert.addButton(withTitle: plan.isStreamCopy ? "Repackage" : "Convert")
407	        alert.addButton(withTitle: "Cancel")
408	        alert.showsSuppressionButton = true
409	        alert.suppressionButton?.title = "Do this automatically from now on"
410	        let accepted = alert.runModal() == .alertFirstButtonReturn
411	        // "From now on" means the answer just given, not always yes: a user
412	        // who cancels with the box ticked is asking never to see this again.
413	        if alert.suppressionButton?.state == .on { remember(accepted ? .always : .never) }
414	        return accepted
415	    }

417	    // MARK: - Orchestration
418	
419	    /// The whole opt-in step: a file AVFoundation refused goes in, a file it
420	    /// can open comes out.
421	    ///
422	    /// * `nil` — no help is available or none was wanted (no ffmpeg, the
423	    ///   policy says no, the user cancelled, ffprobe found nothing to
424	    ///   import). The caller reports AVFoundation's own failure, which is
425	    ///   exactly the behaviour of a machine with no ffmpeg on it.
426	    /// * a URL — a movie on disk under the `.mov` digest name (MP4-format
427	    ///   for a VP9 copy), ready to probe.
428	    /// * a throw — the conversion was authorised and failed, which is worth
429	    ///   its own message rather than "could not read".
430	    ///
431	    /// Synchronous and long by design (`longestAssist` is its bound): it is
432	    /// called from `MediaImporter`'s two synchronous faces, OUTSIDE the
433	    /// 30-second ceiling those put on the AVFoundation probe, because a
434	    /// transcode legitimately takes minutes and being killed at 30 seconds
435	    /// would be a bug rather than a safeguard. `mayAsk` is the CALLER's (spec
436	    /// §11 MC-5): false for a tool call's import, where nobody is at the
437	    /// keyboard, so there the stored policy decides alone and `ask` means no.
438	    ///
439	    /// `reencodingVP9` is the second attempt after a VP9 copy failed, failed
440	    /// its frame check or would not open (spec §11 #227): it answers `nil`
441	    /// for a source whose plan is not a VP9 copy before any question, and
442	    /// re-encodes the video, once per file: a re-encode this process made
443	    /// and kept is answered instead of discarded. `planned` is the first
444	    /// attempt's plan, set before its question, which the second attempt
445	    /// takes instead of running ffprobe again.
446	    static func assist(
447	        _ source: URL, mayAsk: Bool, planned: inout Plan?, reencodingVP9: Bool = false
448	    ) throws -> URL? {
449	        // Before ffmpeg is even looked for, and before the policy is even
450	        // read: a conversion already on disk is already paid for. The policy
451	        // governs whether ffmpeg RUNS, and reusing a finished file runs
452	        // nothing — a user who turned the feature off to stop being asked
453	        // should still get the copy they made last week.
454	        if !reencodingVP9, let existing = existingRewrap(of: source) { return existing }
455	
456	        // Read once, and read BEFORE ffprobe is spawned: a user who said
457	        // never, and a tool call's import with nobody to ask, should cost
458	        // nothing beyond the `stat` above.
459	        let decided = policy
460	        if decided == .never || (decided == .ask && !mayAsk) { return nil }
461	        guard let tools = tools(),
462	            var plan = (reencodingVP9 ? planned : nil) ?? plan(for: source, with: tools)
463	        else { return nil }
464	        if reencodingVP9 {
465	            guard plan.copiesVP9 else { return nil }
466	            plan = plan.reencodingVideo()
467	        } else {
468	            planned = plan
469	        }
470	        if decided == .ask, !consent(for: plan) { return nil }
471	
472	        // The lock starts HERE and not above. Consent can block on the main
473	        // thread, and the main thread can itself be inside this function
474	        // (`ProjectDocument.read(from:ofType:)` is allowed to run there) — so
475	        // a lock held across the alert would be a background thread waiting
476	        // for main while main waits for the lock. Two imports of the same
477	        // file may therefore both ask; the second finds the finished file on
478	        // the re-check below and never runs ffmpeg twice.
479	        conversionLock.lock()
480	        defer { conversionLock.unlock() }
481	        if reencodingVP9 {
482	            // Another import of this file may have re-encoded it while this
483	            // one waited: that file is kept, not discarded (spec §11 #227).
484	            if isKeptReencode(plan.destination) { return plan.destination }
485	            discard(plan.destination)
486	        } else if FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: plan.destination.path) {
487	            return plan.destination
488	        }
489	        let made = try convert(plan, with: tools)
490	        if reencodingVP9 { noteReencode(made) }
491	        return made
492	    }

494	    // MARK: - Running ffmpeg
495	
496	    private static func convert(_ plan: Plan, with tools: Tools) throws -> URL {
497	        let manager = FileManager.default
498	        guard (try? AppSupport.ensureDirectory(plan.destination.deletingLastPathComponent()))
499	            != nil
500	        else {
501	            throw RewrapError.failed(plan.source, "the conversion folder could not be created")
502	        }
503	
504	        // Written under a partial name and moved into place, so a crash, a
505	        // kill or a full disk leaves no truncated file that `existingRewrap`
506	        // would later hand out as finished.
507	        let partial = plan.destination.deletingPathExtension()
508	            .appendingPathExtension("partial.mov")
509	        try? manager.removeItem(at: partial)
510	
511	        let result: ToolResult
512	        do {
513	            result = try run(
514	                tools.ffmpeg, arguments(for: plan, with: tools, writing: partial),
515	                timeout: timeout(for: plan))
516	        } catch let failure as ToolFailure {
517	            try? manager.removeItem(at: partial)
518	            throw failure.timedOut
519	                ? RewrapError.timedOut(plan.source)
520	                : RewrapError.failed(plan.source, failure.detail)
521	        }
522	        guard result.status == 0, manager.fileExists(atPath: partial.path) else {
523	            try? manager.removeItem(at: partial)
524	            throw RewrapError.failed(plan.source, lastLine(of: result.errorOutput))
525	        }
526	        // A VP9 copy is kept only when every frame is on its rate's grid
527	        // (spec §11 #227), checked here so no unchecked copy ever holds the
528	        // name `existingRewrap` hands out.
529	        let exact = !plan.copiesVP9 || keepsFrameGrid(partial, of: plan, with: tools)
530	        guard exact else {
531	            try? manager.removeItem(at: partial)
532	            throw RewrapError.failed(plan.source, "")
533	        }
534	        do {
535	            try manager.moveItem(at: partial, to: plan.destination)
536	        } catch {
537	            try? manager.removeItem(at: partial)
538	            throw RewrapError.failed(plan.source, error.localizedDescription)
539	        }
540	        return plan.destination
541	    }

543	    /// Asked once per process, and only on the transcode path — a stream copy
544	    /// never needs an encoder, and spawning a process to find that out would
545	    /// tax the common case for nothing. Takes `tools` rather than calling
546	    /// `tools()`: this runs inside `convert`, and the two functions must not
547	    /// contend for the same lock (`stateLock` here, `conversionLock` there).
548	    static func hasLibX264(_ tools: Tools) -> Bool {
549	        stateLock.lock()
550	        defer { stateLock.unlock() }
551	        if let known = libX264 { return known }
552	        let result = try? run(
553	            tools.ffmpeg, ["-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-encoders"],
554	            timeout: encoderQueryTimeout)
555	        let text = String(decoding: result?.output ?? Data(), as: UTF8.self)
556	        let found = text.split(separator: "\n").contains { line in
557	            line.split(separator: " ").contains("libx264")
558	        }
559	        libX264 = found
560	        return found
561	    }

563	    /// How long ffmpeg gets. Generous, because the user consented to the
564	    /// cost and a slow disk is not a failure — but bounded, because a hung
565	    /// ffmpeg would otherwise hold the import path for ever. A copy is I/O
566	    /// and finishes in about the time it takes to read the file; an encode
567	    /// runs at some multiple of real time.
568	    private static func timeout(for plan: Plan) -> TimeInterval {
569	        let duration = max(0, plan.duration)
570	        let ceiling = plan.isStreamCopy ? max(300, duration * 2) : max(1800, duration * 30)
571	        return min(ceiling, longestConversion)
572	    }

574	    /// The longest ffmpeg is ever given; `import_media`'s wait covers two
575	    /// (`longestAssist`).
576	    static let longestConversion: TimeInterval = 4 * 3600
577	
578	    private static func lastLine(of data: Data) -> String {
579	        let text = String(decoding: data, as: UTF8.self)
580	        let lines = text.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline).map {
581	            $0.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
582	        }
583	        return lines.last(where: { !$0.isEmpty }) ?? ""
584	    }

586	    // MARK: - Process plumbing
587	
588	    struct ToolResult {
589	        let status: Int32
590	        let output: Data
591	        let errorOutput: Data
592	    }
593	
594	    /// Runs one tool with an argument ARRAY and no shell between here and it,
595	    /// which is the only reason a file named with a semicolon or a backtick
596	    /// is harmless.
597	    ///
598	    /// Both pipes are drained on their own queues while the process runs:
599	    /// reading them after `waitUntilExit` deadlocks the moment ffmpeg writes
600	    /// more than a pipe buffer's worth of diagnostics, which a long encode
601	    /// certainly does.
602	    static func run(_ tool: URL, _ arguments: [String], timeout: TimeInterval) throws
603	        -> ToolResult {
604	        let process = Process()
605	        process.executableURL = tool
606	        process.arguments = arguments
607	        // No terminal, and nothing for a tool to read: a child that blocks on
608	        // stdin would otherwise hang until the timeout.
609	        process.standardInput = FileHandle.nullDevice
610	        let outPipe = Pipe()
611	        let errPipe = Pipe()
612	        process.standardOutput = outPipe
613	        process.standardError = errPipe
614	
615	        let collected = OutputBox()
616	        let drained = DispatchGroup()
617	        let exited = DispatchSemaphore(value: 0)
618	        process.terminationHandler = { _ in exited.signal() }
619	
620	        do {
621	            try process.run()
622	        } catch {
623	            throw ToolFailure(detail: error.localizedDescription, timedOut: false)
624	        }
625	        for (pipe, isError) in [(outPipe, false), (errPipe, true)] {
626	            drained.enter()
627	            DispatchQueue.global(qos: .utility).async {
628	                collected.append(pipe.fileHandleForReading.readDataToEndOfFile(), isError: isError)
629	                drained.leave()
630	            }
631	        }
632	
633	        if exited.wait(timeout: .now() + timeout) != .success {
634	            process.terminate()
635	            if exited.wait(timeout: .now() + runGrace / 2) != .success, process.isRunning {
636	                kill(process.processIdentifier, SIGKILL)
637	            }
638	            _ = drained.wait(timeout: .now() + runGrace / 2)
639	            throw ToolFailure(
640	                detail: "\(tool.lastPathComponent) did not finish in time", timedOut: true)
641	        }
642	        process.waitUntilExit()
643	        _ = drained.wait(timeout: .now() + runGrace / 2)
644	        return ToolResult(
645	            status: process.terminationStatus, output: collected.output,
646	            errorOutput: collected.errorOutput)
647	    }

649	    /// Two background readers write into one of these; the caller reads it
650	    /// only after both have finished, and the lock covers the overlap.
651	    private final class OutputBox {
652	        private let boxLock = NSLock()
653	        private var out = Data()
654	        private var err = Data()
655	
656	        func append(_ data: Data, isError: Bool) {
657	            boxLock.lock()
658	            defer { boxLock.unlock() }
659	            if isError { err.append(data) } else { out.append(data) }
660	        }
661	
662	        var output: Data {
663	            boxLock.lock()
664	            defer { boxLock.unlock() }
665	            return out
666	        }
667	
668	        var errorOutput: Data {
669	            boxLock.lock()
670	            defer { boxLock.unlock() }
671	            return err
672	        }
673	    }
674	
675	    /// A once-computed answer that is allowed to be "no" — `Optional` alone
676	    /// could not tell "not looked yet" from "looked, found nothing".
677	    private final class Box {
678	        let value: Tools?
679	        init(_ value: Tools?) { self.value = value }
680	    }
681	
682	    /// Guards the two once-computed answers below. Held only across a `stat`
683	    /// sweep or one short `-encoders` call, never across a conversion.
684	    private static let stateLock = NSLock()
685	    private static var resolvedTools: Box?
686	    private static var libX264: Bool?
687	
688	    /// Serialises the conversions themselves, so two imports of one file
689	    /// cannot write the same destination at the same time. Deliberately a
690	    /// SECOND lock: `assist` holds this one for the length of an ffmpeg run,
691	    /// and `hasLibX264` runs inside that — one lock for both would deadlock
692	    /// on the first transcode.
693	    private static let conversionLock = NSLock()
694	}

13	    /// What ffmpeg would be asked to do, and what it would cost. Built from
14	    /// ffprobe before anything is asked of the user, because "make the cost
15	    /// obvious before it starts" is the difference between a helpful step and
16	    /// an app that disappears for twenty minutes.
17	    struct Plan {
18	        let source: URL
19	        let destination: URL
20	        /// ffprobe's `codec_name` for the first stream of each type, or nil
21	        /// when the container has none.
22	        let videoCodec: String?
23	        let audioCodec: String?
24	        /// Whether that stream can be copied rather than re-encoded.
25	        let copiesVideo: Bool
26	        let copiesAudio: Bool
27	        let width: Int
28	        let height: Int
29	        let fps: Double
30	        let duration: Double
31	        let sourceBytes: Int64
32	        /// The first video stream's `r_frame_rate`; nil when it is not two
33	        /// positive integers.
34	        let videoRate: FrameRate?
35	
36	        /// The one plan written as MP4, snapped to its frame rate and checked
37	        /// before it is kept (spec §11 #227).
38	        var copiesVP9: Bool { copiesVideo && videoCodec == "vp9" }
39	
40	        /// This plan with the video re-encoded: what a VP9 copy that failed
41	        /// falls back to. The sound is decided again, for a QuickTime file.
42	        func reencodingVideo() -> Plan {
43	            Plan(
44	                source: source, destination: destination, videoCodec: videoCodec,
45	                audioCodec: audioCodec, copiesVideo: false,
46	                copiesAudio: audioCodec.map { FFmpegRewrap.copyableAudio.contains($0) } ?? true,
47	                width: width, height: height, fps: fps, duration: duration,
48	                sourceBytes: sourceBytes, videoRate: videoRate)
49	        }
50	
51	        /// No re-encoding at all: the fast, lossless case, and the one this
52	        /// feature exists for.
53	        var isStreamCopy: Bool { copiesVideo && copiesAudio }
54	
55	        /// Roughly what the result will weigh. A copy is the source's own
56	        /// size; an encode is estimated at 0.12 bits per pixel per frame plus
57	        /// the AAC bitrate, which is the right order of magnitude for the
58	        /// x264 CRF used below and is presented as "about", never as fact.
59	        var estimatedBytes: Int64 {
60	            if copiesVideo { return sourceBytes }
61	            let pixels = Double(max(1, width * height))
62	            let rate = fps > 0 ? fps : 30
63	            let bitsPerSecond = pixels * rate * 0.12 + (copiesAudio ? 0 : 256_000)
64	            let seconds = duration > 0 ? duration : 0
65	            return Int64((bitsPerSecond * seconds / 8).rounded())
66	        }
67	
68	        /// The sentence the user reads before deciding. Names the codec that
69	        /// forced the choice, so "why is this one slow and that one instant"
70	        /// has an answer on screen.
71	        var consentText: String {
72	            let size = ByteCountFormatter.string(fromByteCount: estimatedBytes, countStyle: .file)
73	            let tail =
74	                "\n\nThe original file is left exactly where it is; Frame Job imports the "
75	                + "converted copy from its Application Support folder."
76	            if isStreamCopy {
77	                return "\(source.lastPathComponent) is in a container AVFoundation will not open, "
78	                    + "but the \(codecList) inside it can be decoded as they are. ffmpeg can "
79	                    + "repackage it into a QuickTime movie by copying the streams — no "
80	                    + "re-encoding, no loss of quality, about \(size) and a few seconds."
81	                    + tail
82	            }
83	            if copiesVideo {
84	                // `copiesVideo` is also true when there is no picture at all
85	                // — an audio-only Matroska — and promising to copy a video
86	                // stream that does not exist would be a small lie.
87	                let sound = "\(audioCodec ?? "audio") soundtrack has to be re-encoded to AAC"
88	                let middle = videoCodec == nil
89	                    ? "The \(sound)"
90	                    : "The video can be copied as it is, but the \(sound)"
91	                return "\(source.lastPathComponent) is in a container AVFoundation will not open. "
92	                    + "\(middle). About \(size), and a few seconds."
93	                    + tail
94	            }
95	            return "\(source.lastPathComponent) is \(videoCodec ?? "in a format") this Mac cannot "
96	                + "decode, so repackaging is not enough — the whole file has to be re-encoded to "
97	                + "H.264. That is \(sizeLine) of video and takes at least as long as the clip "
98	                + "runs, usually longer. The result will be about \(size)."
99	                + tail
100	        }
101	
102	        private var codecList: String {
103	            switch (videoCodec, audioCodec) {
104	            case (let video?, let audio?): return "\(video) video and \(audio) audio"
105	            case (let video?, nil): return "\(video) video"
106	            case (nil, let audio?): return "\(audio) audio"
107	            case (nil, nil): return "streams"
108	            }
109	        }
110	
111	        private var sizeLine: String {
112	            let seconds = Int(duration.rounded())
113	            let clock = String(format: "%d:%02d", seconds / 60, seconds % 60)
114	            guard width > 0, height > 0 else { return clock }
115	            return "\(width)×\(height), \(clock)"
116	        }

119	    /// Video codecs a QuickTime file can carry and this Mac can decode, so
120	    /// the stream is copied rather than re-encoded. Conservative on purpose:
121	    /// a codec wrongly listed here produces a `.mov` that AVFoundation opens
122	    /// and then cannot play, which is a far worse failure than a needless
123	    /// re-encode. VP8 and AV1 are deliberately absent — AVFoundation has no
124	    /// QuickTime mapping for either. VP9 is not listed either: its copy is
125	    /// decided by `vp9CopyProfiles` and the stream's frame rate, written as
126	    /// MP4 and checked (spec §11 #227).
127	    private static let copyableVideo: Set<String> = [
128	        "h264", "hevc", "prores", "mjpeg", "mpeg4", "qtrle", "dvvideo",
129	    ]
130	
131	    /// Audio codecs likewise. Opus, Vorbis, FLAC, AC-3 and MP3 are absent:
132	    /// re-encoding a soundtrack is seconds even for a long file, so the
133	    /// benefit of the doubt is not worth a silent track.
134	    private static let copyableAudio: Set<String> = [
135	        "aac", "alac", "pcm_s16le", "pcm_s24le", "pcm_s32le", "pcm_f32le", "pcm_s16be",
136	        "pcm_s24be",
137	    ]
138	
139	    /// The VP9 profiles whose stream is copied rather than re-encoded (spec
140	    /// §11 #227): the two this Mac's supplemental decoder plays (#216).
141	    static let vp9CopyProfiles: Set<Int> = [0, 2]
142	
143	    /// Audio codecs copied beside a VP9 copy, whose file is MP4-format;
144	    /// everything else there is re-encoded to AAC.
145	    private static let mp4CopyableAudio: Set<String> = ["aac", "alac"]

147	    /// Inspects `source` and decides copy versus encode per stream. `nil`
148	    /// when ffprobe cannot read the file or finds nothing to import — a
149	    /// container with no video and no audio is not something ffmpeg can
150	    /// rescue, and the caller's own "no video or audio the app can open"
151	    /// message is the better one.
152	    static func plan(for source: URL, with tools: Tools) -> Plan? {
153	        guard let destination = destination(for: source) else { return nil }
154	        let arguments = [
155	            "-v", "error", "-print_format", "json", "-show_streams", "-show_format",
156	            source.path,
157	        ]
158	        guard let result = try? run(tools.ffprobe, arguments, timeout: planTimeout),
159	            result.status == 0,
160	            let root = (try? JSONSerialization.jsonObject(with: result.output)) as? [String: Any]
161	        else { return nil }
162	
163	        let streams = (root["streams"] as? [[String: Any]]) ?? []
164	        let format = (root["format"] as? [String: Any]) ?? [:]
165	        let video = streams.first { $0["codec_type"] as? String == "video" }
166	        let audio = streams.first { $0["codec_type"] as? String == "audio" }
167	        // An attached cover image is a video stream with a still disposition;
168	        // importing it as the picture would be wrong, so it does not count.
169	        let isCover = ((video?["disposition"] as? [String: Any])?["attached_pic"] as? Int) == 1
170	        let videoCodec = isCover ? nil : video?["codec_name"] as? String
171	        let audioCodec = audio?["codec_name"] as? String
172	        guard videoCodec != nil || audioCodec != nil else { return nil }
173	        // A VP9 stream is copied only for a profile this Mac decodes and a
174	        // rate the copy can be snapped to; the copy itself is checked later
175	        // (`keepsFrameGrid`).
176	        let videoRate = isCover ? nil : frameRate(video?["r_frame_rate"] as? String)
177	        let copiesVP9 = videoCodec == "vp9" && videoRate != nil
178	            && (profile(video?["profile"]).map { vp9CopyProfiles.contains($0) } ?? false)
179	        let audioSet = copiesVP9 ? mp4CopyableAudio : copyableAudio
180	
181	        return Plan(
182	            source: source, destination: destination, videoCodec: videoCodec,
183	            audioCodec: audioCodec,
184	            copiesVideo: videoCodec.map { copiesVP9 || copyableVideo.contains($0) } ?? true,
185	            copiesAudio: audioCodec.map { audioSet.contains($0) } ?? true,
186	            width: isCover ? 0 : (video?["width"] as? Int) ?? 0,
187	            height: isCover ? 0 : (video?["height"] as? Int) ?? 0,
188	            fps: rate(video?["avg_frame_rate"] as? String),
189	            duration: Double(format["duration"] as? String ?? "") ?? 0,
190	            sourceBytes: Int64(format["size"] as? String ?? "") ?? 0,
191	            videoRate: videoRate)
192	    }

195	    /// (`"Profile 0"`); anything else is unknown.

214	        guard let parts = text?.split(separator: "/"), parts.count == 2,
215	            let num = Double(parts[0]), let den = Double(parts[1]), den > 0

226	    static func arguments(for plan: Plan, with tools: Tools, writing output: URL)

244	                if plan.copiesVP9, let rate = plan.videoRate {

260	    /// The frame check (spec §11 #227): whether every video packet of
261	    /// `file`, a VP9 copy, sits a whole number of frames after the first, and
262	    /// the first a whole number of frames from zero, at `plan.videoRate`.
263	    /// Read from the file with ffprobe, because ffmpeg's exit code does not
264	    /// say. Anything unreadable is false. Takes no lock: it runs inside
265	    /// `convert`. The arithmetic is `onFrameGrid`'s.
266	    static func keepsFrameGrid(_ file: URL, of plan: Plan, with tools: Tools) -> Bool {
267	        guard let rate = plan.videoRate else { return false }
268	        let arguments = [
269	            "-v", "error", "-select_streams", "v:0", "-show_entries",
270	            "stream=time_base:packet=pts", "-of", "csv=p=0", file.path,
271	        ]
272	        guard let result = try? run(tools.ffprobe, arguments, timeout: frameCheckTimeout),
273	            result.status == 0
274	        else { return false }
275	        var timescale: Int64?
276	        var times: [Int64] = []
277	        let text = String(decoding: result.output, as: UTF8.self)
278	        for line in text.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline) {
279	            let entry = line.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespaces)
280	            if entry.isEmpty { continue }
281	            if entry.hasPrefix("1/") {
282	                guard timescale == nil, let value = Int64(entry.dropFirst(2)), value > 0
283	                else { return false }
284	                timescale = value
285	            } else if let pts = Int64(entry) {
286	                times.append(pts)
287	            } else {
288	                return false
289	            }
290	        }
291	        guard let timescale else { return false }
292	        return onFrameGrid(times: times, timescale: timescale, rate: rate)
293	    }
294	
295	    /// Whether `times`, packet times in units of 1/`timescale` s, are
296	    /// consecutive frames at `rate`: the first a whole number of frames from
297	    /// zero and each next one exactly one frame later. Pure. No packet, a
298	    /// frame that is not a whole number of units, or a next time past
299	    /// `Int64.max` is false; the next time is computed only before a further
300	    /// packet, so a last packet near the top of the range is not an overflow.
301	    static func onFrameGrid(times: [Int64], timescale: Int64, rate: FrameRate) -> Bool {
302	        guard let first = times.first, first >= 0 else { return false }
303	        let (ticks, overflow) = timescale.multipliedReportingOverflow(by: Int64(rate.den))
304	        guard !overflow, ticks % Int64(rate.num) == 0 else { return false }
305	        let step = ticks / Int64(rate.num)
306	        guard step > 0, first % step == 0 else { return false }
307	        var expected = first
308	        for pts in times.dropFirst() {
309	            let (next, past) = expected.addingReportingOverflow(step)
310	            guard !past else { return false }
311	            guard pts == next else { return false }
312	            expected = next
313	        }
314	        return true
315	    }

318	
319	    /// ffprobe's read of a source's streams (`plan`).
320	    static let planTimeout: TimeInterval = 20
321	    /// ffprobe's read of a VP9 copy's packet times (`keepsFrameGrid`).
322	    static let frameCheckTimeout: TimeInterval = 300
323	    /// ffmpeg's `-encoders` listing (`hasLibX264`).
324	    static let encoderQueryTimeout: TimeInterval = 20
325	    /// What `run` adds to any tool's own timeout: half for the tool to exit
326	    /// after `terminate`, half for its two pipes to drain.
327	    static let runGrace: TimeInterval = 20
328	
329	    /// The longest one import's ffmpeg step can take, both attempts (spec
330	    /// §11 #227): one plan (the second attempt takes the first's), the frame
331	    /// check, the encoder query, two conversions — the VP9 copy, then its
332	    /// re-encode — and `run`'s grace on each of those five runs.
333	    /// `import_media`'s wait is this plus its header probes
334	    /// (`AgentServer.probeCeiling`).
335	    static var longestAssist: TimeInterval {
336	        planTimeout + frameCheckTimeout + encoderQueryTimeout + 2 * longestConversion
337	            + 5 * runGrace
338	    }

397	/// A WebM or Matroska file opened by a built-in rewrap (spec §11 #216-R):
398	/// the core indexes the container (`ReelContainer`) and its first video and
399	/// audio streams are copied, unchanged, into a QuickTime movie under
400	/// `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Rewrapped/`, the folder ffmpeg's
401	/// conversions use, by `FFmpegRewrap.destination(for:)`'s digest name — so a
402	/// second import of the same file reuses the copy.
403	///
404	/// The order is the decision's: the core opens the file; a codec this Mac
405	/// cannot decode is refused in #216's sentence BEFORE anything is copied
406	/// (VP8, AV1 without hardware decode, VP9 Profile 1 or 3), and a codec the
407	/// copy cannot carry is refused in its own (`unsupported`), which alone
408	/// falls through to the opt-in ffmpeg step; the video is snapped to its
409	/// frame grid when it lies on one; the copy's size is checked against the
410	/// free space first; and the movie is written under a `.partial.mov` name
411	/// and moved into place, so a failure leaves no file behind.
412	///
413	/// Await-free (spec §11 W-8): `ContainerRewrapWriter` waits on its writer
414	/// through a semaphore.
415	enum ContainerRewrap {
416	
417	    /// Whether `url` begins with an EBML header: 1A 45 DF A3.
418	    static func isMatroska(_ url: URL) -> Bool {
419	        guard let handle = try? FileHandle(forReadingFrom: url) else { return false }
420	        defer { try? handle.close() }
421	        let head = (try? handle.read(upToCount: 4)) ?? Data()
422	        return head == Data([0x1A, 0x45, 0xDF, 0xA3])
423	    }
424	
425	    /// Held across the existence re-check and the copy, so two imports of one
426	    /// file copy it once. Never held across a wait on the main thread (a
427	    /// watch only posts to main, and a tool call passes none), so it cannot
428	    /// deadlock against the agent lane's lock (spec §11 #231).
429	    private static let lock = NSLock()
430	
431	    /// The movie for `source`: a copy already on disk, else a new one.
432	    /// `watch` is called once, on this thread, when a new copy starts, with
433	    /// the progress the copy reports to and reads its Cancel from (spec §11
434	    /// #228-P); a reused copy calls none, and a tool call passes none.
435	    static func assist(_ source: URL, watch: RewrapWatch? = nil) throws -> URL {
436	        if let existing = FFmpegRewrap.existingRewrap(of: source) { return existing }
437	        guard let destination = FFmpegRewrap.destination(for: source) else {
438	            throw ContainerRewrapError.failed(source, reason: "the copy folder could not be found")
439	        }
440	        lock.lock()
441	        defer { lock.unlock() }
442	        if FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: destination.path) { return destination }
443	        let progress = RewrapProgress(source: source)
444	        watch?(progress)
445	        defer { progress.finish() }
446	        try rewrap(source, to: destination, progress: progress)
447	        return destination
448	    }
449	
450	    /// Copies `source` into a movie at `destination`. `freeBytes` stands in
451	    /// for the volume's free space, `stopAfter` fails the copy after that
452	    /// many samples and `refuseAudioAt` has the writer refuse that audio
453	    /// sample — the three seams the probe drives; the app passes none.
454	    /// `progress` is told the copy's size and each sample's bytes, and its
455	    /// Cancel is read after the index opens, before the write and between
456	    /// samples; a cancelled copy throws `.cancelled` with nothing left.
457	    static func rewrap(
458	        _ source: URL, to destination: URL, freeBytes: Int64? = nil, stopAfter: Int? = nil,
459	        refuseAudioAt: Int? = nil, progress: RewrapProgress? = nil
460	    ) throws {
461	        let container: ReelContainer
462	        do {
463	            container = try ReelContainer(path: source.path)
464	        } catch {
465	            let reason = (error as? ReelCoreError)?.message ?? error.localizedDescription
466	            throw ContainerRewrapError.unreadable(source, reason: reason)
467	        }
468	        if progress?.isCancelled == true { throw ContainerRewrapError.cancelled(source) }
469	        var description = try describe(container, source)
470	        if description.video == nil, description.audio == nil {
471	            throw MediaImporter.ImportError.noTracks(source)
472	        }
473	        try precheck(description, source)
474	        if let nominal = description.video?.nominalFps {
475	            _ = container.retime(MediaImporter.rationalFrameRate(nominal))
476	            description = try describe(container, source)
477	        }
478	        try checkSpace(for: description, source, at: destination, freeBytes: freeBytes)
479	        if progress?.isCancelled == true { throw ContainerRewrapError.cancelled(source) }
480	        do {
481	            try AppSupport.ensureDirectory(destination.deletingLastPathComponent())
482	        } catch {
483	            throw ContainerRewrapError.failed(source, reason: "the copy folder could not be created")
484	        }
485	        let manager = FileManager.default
486	        let partial = destination.deletingPathExtension().appendingPathExtension("partial.mov")
487	        try? manager.removeItem(at: partial)
488	        progress?.begin(
489	            totalBytes: (description.video?.bytes ?? 0) + (description.audio?.bytes ?? 0))
490	        do {
491	            try ContainerRewrapWriter.write(
492	                container, description, from: source, to: partial, stopAfter: stopAfter,
493	                refuseAudioAt: refuseAudioAt, progress: progress)
494	            try manager.moveItem(at: partial, to: destination)
495	        } catch {
496	            try? manager.removeItem(at: partial)
497	            if error is ContainerRewrapError { throw error }
498	            throw ContainerRewrapError.failed(source, reason: error.localizedDescription)
499	        }
500	    }
501	
502	    private static func describe(
503	        _ container: ReelContainer, _ source: URL
504	    ) throws -> ContainerDescription {
505	        let decoder = JSONDecoder()
506	        decoder.keyDecodingStrategy = .convertFromSnakeCase
507	        guard let description = try? decoder.decode(
508	            ContainerDescription.self, from: Data(container.describeJSON.utf8))
509	        else {
510	            throw ContainerRewrapError.unreadable(source, reason: "its index could not be read")
511	        }
512	        return description
513	    }

516	
517	    /// #216's refusals from the codec facts in the Tracks element, then a
518	    /// codec the copy does not carry.
519	    private static func precheck(_ d: ContainerDescription, _ source: URL) throws {
520	        let fileName = source.lastPathComponent
521	        if let video = d.video, !video.encoded, let fourcc = video.fourcc {
522	            let codec = fourCharCode(fourcc)
523	            let av1Hardware = VTIsHardwareDecodeSupported(kCMVideoCodecType_AV1)
524	            let profile = video.vp9Profile
525	            let undecodable = fourcc == "vp08"
526	                || (codec == kCMVideoCodecType_AV1 && !av1Hardware)
527	                || (codec == kCMVideoCodecType_VP9 && (profile == 1 || profile == 3))
528	            if undecodable {
529	                throw MediaImporter.ImportError.undecodable(
530	                    source,
531	                    sentence: DecoderSupport.refusal(
532	                        fileName: fileName, codec: codec, vp9Profile: profile,
533	                        av1Hardware: av1Hardware))
534	            }
535	        }
536	        let tracks: [(kind: String, codecID: String, fourcc: String?, encoded: Bool)] = [
537	            d.video.map { ("video", $0.codecId, $0.fourcc, $0.encoded) },
538	            d.audio.map { ("audio", $0.codecId, $0.fourcc, $0.encoded) },
539	        ].compactMap { $0 }
540	        for track in tracks where track.fourcc == nil || track.encoded {
541	            throw ContainerRewrapError.unsupported(
542	                source,
543	                sentence: unsupported(
544	                    fileName: fileName, kind: track.kind, codecID: track.codecID,
545	                    encoded: track.encoded))
546	        }
547	    }

549	    /// The free space on the volume the copy goes to, against what the core
550	    /// says the copy needs. With no reading of the volume, the copy goes on.
551	    private static func checkSpace(
552	        for d: ContainerDescription, _ source: URL, at destination: URL, freeBytes: Int64?
553	    ) throws {
554	        var folder = destination.deletingLastPathComponent()
555	        while !FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: folder.path), folder.path != "/" {
556	            folder = folder.deletingLastPathComponent()
557	        }
558	        let values = try? folder.resourceValues(forKeys: [
559	            .volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsageKey, .volumeLocalizedNameKey, .volumeNameKey,
560	        ])
561	        guard let free = freeBytes ?? values?.volumeAvailableCapacityForImportantUsage else {
562	            return
563	        }
564	        let needed = Int64(clamping: d.requiredBytes)
565	        guard free < needed else { return }
566	        let volume = values?.volumeLocalizedName ?? values?.volumeName ?? "the disk"
567	        throw ContainerRewrapError.noSpace(
568	            source,
569	            sentence: spaceRefusal(
570	                fileName: source.lastPathComponent, needed: needed, free: free, volume: volume))
571	    }

689	/// What this Mac can decode, asked of the decoders themselves (spec §11
690	/// #216). macOS ships VP9 and AV1 decoders that a process must opt in to,
691	/// and the opt-in is per process: `enable()` is called at launch, before a
692	/// cache pass, before a composition looks up a track, and in the harness and
693	/// the formats probe. An import then decodes one frame of its video track
694	/// (`decodesFirstFrame`), because `isPlayable` answers yes for files no
695	/// decoder here reads (VP9 Profile 1, AV1 on an M1/M2), and a refusal names
696	/// the codec (`refusal`).
697	///
698	/// Await-free: `AVAssetReader` is synchronous, as in `writePeaks`; `async`
699	/// stays in `MediaImporter.swift` (spec §11 W-8).
700	enum DecoderSupport {
701	
702	    /// The registration, run once by the first `enable()`. A `static let`'s
703	    /// initialiser runs exactly once, on whichever thread gets there first.
704	    private static let registration: Void = {
705	        VTRegisterSupplementalVideoDecoderIfAvailable(kCMVideoCodecType_VP9)
706	        VTRegisterSupplementalVideoDecoderIfAvailable(kCMVideoCodecType_AV1)
707	    }()
708	
709	    /// Opts this process in to the supplemental VP9 and AV1 decoders.
710	    /// Idempotent and callable from any thread.
711	    static func enable() {
712	        _ = registration
713	    }
714	
715	    /// The reader errors that mean "nothing here decodes this": no decoder
716	    /// (-11833), and a decoder that cannot read this format (-11855, VP9
717	    /// Profile 1/3). Every other failure — damaged or truncated data in a
718	    /// codec this Mac decodes (-11821, -11880) — imports as it did before.
719	    static let refusingErrorCodes: Set<Int> = [
720	        AVError.Code.decoderNotFound.rawValue, AVError.Code.undecodableMediaData.rawValue,
721	    ]
722	
723	    /// Whether `track`'s first frame decodes to 32BGRA. False ONLY when the
724	    /// reader fails with one of `refusingErrorCodes`; an image buffer, a
725	    /// track that completes with none, a reader that cannot be made and any
726	    /// other error all answer true. Reads at most until the first image.
727	    static func decodesFirstFrame(of track: AVAssetTrack, in asset: AVAsset) -> Bool {
728	        enable()
729	        guard let reader = try? AVAssetReader(asset: asset) else { return true }
730	        let output = AVAssetReaderTrackOutput(
731	            track: track,
732	            outputSettings: [kCVPixelBufferPixelFormatTypeKey as String: REDACTED])
733	        output.alwaysCopiesSampleData = false
734	        guard reader.canAdd(output) else { return true }
735	        reader.add(output)
736	        defer { reader.cancelReading() }
737	        guard reader.startReading() else { return !refuses(reader.error) }
738	        while let sample = output.copyNextSampleBuffer() {
739	            if CMSampleBufferGetImageBuffer(sample) != nil { return true }
740	        }
741	        // Read the status before the deferred cancel: cancelling first would
742	        // erase the difference between completion and a decoder failure.
743	        return reader.status != .failed || !refuses(reader.error)
744	    }
745	
746	    /// Whether a reader's error is one of the codes that refuse an import.
747	    private static func refuses(_ error: (any Error)?) -> Bool {
748	        guard let error = error as NSError?, error.domain == AVFoundationErrorDomain else {
749	            return false
750	        }
751	        let code = error.code
752	        return Self.refusingErrorCodes.contains(code)
753	    }
754	
755	    /// The `profile` byte of a VP9 description's `vpcC` record: byte 4,
756	    /// after the version byte and three flag bytes. Nil when absent or short.
757	    static func vp9Profile(of description: CMFormatDescription) -> Int? {
758	        guard let atoms = CMFormatDescriptionGetExtension(
759	            description,
760	            extensionKey: kCMFormatDescriptionExtension_SampleDescriptionExtensionAtoms)
761	            as? [String: Any],
762	            let record = atoms["vpcC"] as? Data, record.count > 4
763	        else { return nil }
764	        return Int(record[record.startIndex + 4])
765	    }
766	
767	    /// 'vp08'. CoreMedia names no constant for VP8.
768	    private static let vp8: FourCharCode = 0x7670_3038
769	
770	    /// The refusal sentence for a video track that will not decode.
771	    static func refusal(
772	        fileName: String, codec: FourCharCode, vp9Profile: Int?, av1Hardware: Bool
773	    ) -> String {
774	        switch codec {
775	        case kCMVideoCodecType_AV1 where !av1Hardware:
776	            return "\(fileName) is AV1 video, which needs an M3 or later Mac."
777	        case kCMVideoCodecType_AV1:
778	            return "\(fileName) is AV1 video, which this Mac cannot decode."
779	        case kCMVideoCodecType_VP9:
780	            if let profile = vp9Profile, profile == 1 || profile == 3 {
781	                return "\(fileName) is VP9 Profile \(profile) video, which this Mac cannot decode;"
782	                    + " VP9 Profiles 0 and 2 import."
783	            }
784	            return "\(fileName) is VP9 video, which this Mac cannot decode."
785	        case vp8:
786	            return "\(fileName) is VP8 video, which this Mac cannot decode."
787	        case 0:
788	            return "\(fileName) is video this Mac cannot decode."
789	        default:
790	            let code = String([24, 16, 8, 0].map {
791	                Character(Unicode.Scalar(UInt8((codec >> UInt32($0)) & 0xFF)))
792	            })
793	            return "\(fileName) is '\(code)' video, which this Mac cannot decode."
794	        }
795	    }
796	
797	    /// The sentence for a track with these descriptions: the first one's
798	    /// codec and VP9 profile, and whether this Mac decodes AV1 in hardware.
799	    static func refusal(fileName: String, descriptions: [CMFormatDescription]) -> String {
800	        let first = descriptions.first
801	        return refusal(
802	            fileName: fileName, codec: first.map { CMFormatDescriptionGetMediaSubType($0) } ?? 0,
803	            vp9Profile: first.flatMap { vp9Profile(of: $0) },
804	            av1Hardware: VTIsHardwareDecodeSupported(kCMVideoCodecType_AV1))
805	    }

810	//
811	// A pure move out of `ProjectDocument.swift` (road map 10, G3a), which is

813	// store's lines. `present(_:)`, internal so this file can reach it, lives in

816	import AppKit

818	extension ProjectDocument {
819	    // MARK: - Media import
820	
821	    /// File > Add Media… and every drop that adds files to an OPEN project.
822	    /// Probing is asynchronous, so the files are probed one at a time and the
823	    /// whole batch commits as ONE undo step; `completion` gets the new media
824	    /// ids in the order the files were given, on the main thread.
825	    func importMedia(_ urls: [URL], completion: (([UInt32]) -> Void)? = nil) {
826	        guard !urls.isEmpty else {
827	            completion?([])
828	            return
829	        }
830	        probeNext(urls, index: 0, descriptors: [], completion: completion)
831	    }
832	
833	    private func probeNext(
834	        _ urls: [URL], index: Int, descriptors: [MediaDescriptor],
835	        completion: (([UInt32]) -> Void)?
836	    ) {
837	        guard index < urls.count else {
838	            // Two statements, never `completion?(commitImport(descriptors))`:
839	            // optional chaining skips the ARGUMENT too, so with no completion
840	            // — File ▸ Add Media… and a Media-tab drop pass none — the files
841	            // were probed and never added, with no beep and no error.
842	            let added = commitImport(descriptors)
843	            completion?(added)
844	            return
845	        }
846	        MediaImporter.probe(url: urls[index], mayAsk: true, watch: Self.copyWatch) {
847	            [weak self] result in
848	            guard let self = self else { return }
849	            var collected = descriptors
850	            switch result {
851	            case .success(let descriptor):
852	                collected.append(descriptor)
853	            case .failure(let error) where Self.isCancelledCopy(error):
854	                break  // the person's Cancel: the file is left out, unannounced
855	            case .failure(let error):
856	                // One unreadable file must not lose the rest of the drop.
857	                self.present(error)
858	            }
859	            self.probeNext(
860	                urls, index: index + 1, descriptors: collected, completion: completion)
861	        }
862	    }

877	    /// The Media tab's Relink… and the missing-media sheet's Relink: each
878	    /// chosen file is probed in order through import's own
879	    /// `MediaImporter.probe` (ffmpeg's opt-in step included), an unreadable
880	    /// one is presented and skipped, and every probed relink commits as ONE
881	    /// undo step, then the cache pass. The path and bookmark are the
882	    /// descriptor's — the rewrapped `.mov` when ffmpeg converted — and the
883	    /// core takes the file's duration, size, rate and flags from its probe,
884	    /// refuses a file of another kind in its own sentence, and holds a clip
885	    /// that runs past a shorter file's end to it.
886	    ///
887	    /// `alertingRefusals` is the sheet's (#180): #88's fold answers a list
888	    /// that applied with no refusal, so the ops are tried first on the
889	    /// project as it stands, and after the commit and the cache pass each
890	    /// refused sentence is presented, verbatim and in order. The Media tab
891	    /// passes one op and keeps the default: the fold's beep and CI-10 strip.
892	    /// On both doors an unreadable file is presented at once; `present(_:)`
893	    /// shows each alert in turn.
894	    func relinkMedia(_ choices: [(media: UInt32, url: URL)], alertingRefusals: Bool = false) {
895	        relinkNext(choices, index: 0, ops: [], alertingRefusals: alertingRefusals)
896	    }

898	    private func relinkNext(
899	        _ choices: [(media: UInt32, url: URL)], index: Int, ops: [ReelOp],
900	        alertingRefusals: Bool
901	    ) {
902	        guard index < choices.count else {
903	            guard !ops.isEmpty else { return }
904	            let refusals = alertingRefusals ? relinkRefusals(ops) : []
905	            // The probe's completion is not an AppKit event: the grouped
906	            // entry point is mandatory (app/CLAUDE.md's undo pitfall).
907	            performGroupedEdit("Relink Media", ops)
908	            generateCaches()
909	            for refusal in refusals { present(RelinkRefusalAlert(refusal: refusal)) }
910	            return
911	        }
912	        let choice = choices[index]
913	        MediaImporter.probe(url: choice.url, mayAsk: true, watch: Self.copyWatch) {
914	            [weak self] result in
915	            guard let self = self else { return }
916	            var collected = ops
917	            switch result {
918	            case .success(let probed):
919	                // The cursor file beside the new movie, else the one kept (spec §11 CU-38 (a)).
920	                let descriptor = MediaImporter.relinkProbe(
921	                    probed, current: self.project.snapshot.media(choice.media))
922	                collected.append(
923	                    .relinkMedia(
924	                        media: choice.media, path: descriptor.path,
925	                        bookmark: descriptor.bookmark, probe: descriptor))
926	            case .failure(let error) where Self.isCancelledCopy(error):
927	                break  // the person's Cancel: this relink is left out, unannounced
928	            case .failure(let error):
929	                // One unreadable file must not lose the rest of the sheet.
930	                self.present(error)
931	            }
932	            self.relinkNext(
933	                choices, index: index + 1, ops: collected, alertingRefusals: alertingRefusals)
934	        }
935	    }

937	    /// Every refusal `ops` would meet, in order: walked over `project` as
938	    /// `ReelProject.applying(_:)` walks a list, each op on the last applied
939	    /// result. A throw ends the walk; the commit presents it.
940	    private func relinkRefusals(_ ops: [ReelOp]) -> [ReelRefusal] {
941	        var current = project
942	        var refusals: [ReelRefusal] = []
943	        for op in ops {
944	            guard let edit = try? current.applying(op) else { break }
945	            switch edit {
946	            case .applied(let next): current = next
947	            case .identity: break
948	            case .refused(let refusal): refusals.append(refusal)
949	            }
950	        }
951	        return refusals
952	    }

994	/// The open-time repairs of a project's media, after `project.json` is read
995	/// and before the document is shown: the re-anchor of consolidated media
996	/// (`ProjectDocument.reanchoringConsolidatedMedia`) and, here, the re-copy
997	/// of a WebM or Matroska copy that is gone (spec §11 #228-O, O13 and Q3).
998	///
999	/// Neither is an edit. Both run where `readPackage` runs — on
1000	/// NSDocumentController's read queue for a person's File ▸ Open, on the
1001	/// lane's thread inside `withoutAsking` for an agent's `open_project` (spec
1002	/// §11 #231), on the main thread for a read AppKit runs there — before the
1003	/// document exists as far as AppKit is concerned, so they register no undo
1004	/// step, dirty nothing and show no alert; whatever save comes next writes
1005	/// the new paths out.
1006	extension ProjectDocument {
1007	
1008	    /// `readPackage`'s repairs, in order: the re-anchor first, so a
1009	    /// consolidated copy found in the package's `media/` is never copied
1010	    /// again, then the cursor files' re-anchor (spec §11 CU-52), then the
1011	    /// re-copy.
1012	    static func repairingMedia(_ project: ReelProject, package: URL) -> ReelProject {
1013	        let anchored = reanchoringConsolidatedMedia(project, package: package)
1014	        let cursors = reanchoringCursorFiles(anchored, package: package)
1015	        return recopyingMissingCopies(cursors)
1016	    }

1018	    /// Points each media's cursor file at the package's `media/` when it was
1019	    /// consolidated there and the package has moved (road map creator-jobs
1020	    /// CU5, spec §11 CU-52): a `media.cursor` whose `cursorURL(for:)` names no
1021	    /// file, while `<package>/media/<its path's last component>` exists, gets
1022	    /// `set_media_cursor {path: that file, in_picture}` — no bookmark, as
1023	    /// Consolidate writes it. Applied purely, as the media re-anchor is.
1024	    static func reanchoringCursorFiles(_ project: ReelProject, package: URL) -> ReelProject {
1025	        // `media/`, `ProjectDocument`'s private `mediaDirectoryName`, which this
1026	        // extension in another file cannot read (`ProjectDocument.swift` takes
1027	        // no line for CU5).
1028	        let directory = package.appendingPathComponent("media", isDirectory: true)
1029	        guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: directory.path) else { return project }
1030	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
1031	        for media in project.snapshot.media {
1032	            guard let cursor = media.cursor, let file = cursorURL(for: media),
1033	                !FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: file.path)
1034	            else { continue }
1035	            let name = (cursor.path as NSString).lastPathComponent
1036	            guard !name.isEmpty else { continue }
1037	            let candidate = directory.appendingPathComponent(name)
1038	            guard FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: candidate.path) else { continue }
1039	            ops.append(
1040	                .setMediaCursor(
1041	                    media: media.id,
1042	                    cursor: MediaCursor(path: candidate.path, inPicture: cursor.inPicture)))
1043	        }
1044	        guard !ops.isEmpty else { return project }
1045	        // Only `.applied` is a repair; both other arms leave it as opened.
1046	        return (try? project.applying(ops)).project ?? project
1047	    }

1049	    /// Copies again every WebM or Matroska copy that is gone, from its
1050	    /// original, and points the media at the new copy with its probe.
1051	    ///
1052	    /// A media is copied again when all four hold: its copy is gone —
1053	    /// `mediaURL(for:)` resolves nothing, or resolves inside the Trash
1054	    /// (`trashed`), where Finder's delete moves the copy and its bookmark
1055	    /// follows it; it has an `original`; the original resolves; and the
1056	    /// original is still a Matroska file. The copy is the built-in one only
1057	    /// (`MediaImporter.probeBuiltInCopy`): never ffmpeg, never a question.
1058	    /// The Trash counts as gone HERE only; every other reader of
1059	    /// `mediaURL(for:)` still plays a copy from the Trash.
1060	    ///
1061	    /// Each copy shows #228-P's window after 1 s through `watch`, except on
1062	    /// the main thread, where a window could not be shown, and inside
1063	    /// `withoutAsking`, an agent's `open_project` (MC-5, #231): no watch is
1064	    /// passed there. Copies run one at a time (`ContainerRewrap.assist`'s
1065	    /// lock). A Cancel or any failure skips that media (Q3): a missing copy
1066	    /// stays missing, with the slate, the badge and Relink…, and the next
1067	    /// open tries again; a copy in the Trash keeps its path and bookmark.
1068	    ///
1069	    /// `trashed` is the probe's seam, so the Trash case is proved without
1070	    /// touching the real Trash; the app passes none.
1071	    static func recopyingMissingCopies(
1072	        _ project: ReelProject, watch: RewrapWatch? = RewrapProgressWindowController.watch,
1073	        trashed: (URL) -> Bool = isTrashed
1074	    ) -> ReelProject {
1075	        let shown = Thread.isMainThread || MediaImporter.isWithoutAsking ? nil : watch
1076	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
1077	        for media in project.snapshot.media where media.original != nil {
1078	            let copy = mediaURL(for: media)
1079	            guard copy == nil || copy.map(trashed) == true else { continue }
1080	            guard let source = originalURL(for: media), ContainerRewrap.isMatroska(source) else {
1081	                continue
1082	            }
1083	            guard let copied = try? MediaImporter.probeBuiltInCopy(of: source, watch: shown)
1084	            else { continue }
1085	            let descriptor = MediaImporter.relinkProbe(copied, current: media)  // CU-38 (a)
1086	            ops.append(
1087	                .relinkMedia(
1088	                    media: media.id, path: descriptor.path, bookmark: descriptor.bookmark,
1089	                    probe: descriptor))
1090	        }
1091	        guard !ops.isEmpty else { return project }
1092	        // Only `.applied` is a repair; both other arms leave it as opened.
1093	        return (try? project.applying(ops)).project ?? project
1094	    }

1	## Bringing files in
2	
3	### What Frame Job reads
4	
5	| Kind | Files |
6	|---|---|
7	| Movies | MOV, MP4, M4V and other containers macOS plays: H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG and MPEG-4 video; VP9 Profile 0 and 2 in MP4; AV1 on an M3 or later Mac. |
8	| WebM and Matroska | `.webm` and `.mkv` with VP9, AV1, H.264 or HEVC video and Opus, Vorbis or AAC sound (see below). |
9	| Sound | M4A (AAC, ALAC), MP3, WAV and AIFF everywhere. Other formats macOS plays, such as CAF and FLAC, import when dropped on the Media tab. |
10	| Pictures | PNG, JPEG and HEIC everywhere. TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP also import when dropped on the Media tab. |
11	| LUTs | `.cube` 3D LUTs, applied as a clip's look or as a file's Camera Log. See [Color grading](color-grading.md). |
12	
13	Caption files (`.srt`) are not media: bring them in with **File ▸ Import Captions…**. See [Captions](captions.md).
14	
15	### Add Media
16	
17	**File ▸ Add Media…** (⇧⌘I), or the Media tab's **Add Media…** button, opens a panel for one or more files. Every file is checked first. The readable ones are added to the Media tab together as one undo step ("Add Media", or "Add 3 Media Files"). A file that cannot be read shows an alert naming it, and the rest are still added. Adding a file that is already in the list changes nothing.
18	
19	Adding puts files in the Media tab, **not** on the timeline. Place them from there (see [Putting media on the timeline](#putting-media-on-the-timeline)).
20	
21	You can also drag files from the Finder onto the **Media tab**. That adds them to this project. A Finder drop anywhere else on the window (the canvas, the timeline) *opens* the file as a project of its own, as a drop on the Dock icon does.
22	
23	*Agents:* `import_media` (takes a `path`; answers the new media id and what the check found: kind, duration, display size, frame rate, video/audio/alpha). `add_media` is the raw op behind it, taking a descriptor you supply.
24	
25	### WebM and Matroska files
26	
27	macOS cannot play WebM or MKV directly, so Frame Job copies the video and sound streams into a movie, without re-encoding, the first time you add or open one. The copy goes into `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Rewrapped/`; your original is left where it is.
28	
29	- There is no question to answer. A copy that takes more than a second shows a small **Copying Movie** window with its progress, and **Cancel** stops it and adds nothing.
30	- Before copying, Frame Job checks the disk has room. If it does not: "Not enough free space to open *file*: its video and sound need about *size* on "*volume*", which has *size* free. Nothing was copied."
31	- The copy keeps the colour the file states: HLG, HDR10 (PQ), or a BT.709, BT.601 or BT.2020 SDR picture, read from the file's colour information or, for VP9, from the video itself. A file that states none is shown as macOS reads it.
32	- Importing the same file again reuses the copy.
33	- The media keeps the original's name, and its tooltip on the Media tab says where the copy lives.
34	- If the copy is later deleted, or moved to the Trash, the project makes it again from the original the next time it opens. If that copy is cancelled or fails, the file shows as missing (a slate, the **missing** badge, Relink…) until the next open tries again.
35	- Frame Job never deletes anything from the Rewrapped folder, which every project shares, so copies pile up there. You can clear it: WebM and MKV copies are made again on the next open (ffmpeg conversions are not; see below).
36	- **Consolidate Media** copies the copy, not the WebM, into the package's `media/` folder, and the row's tooltip then says it was copied into this project's package.
37	
38	A stream the built-in copy cannot carry (FLAC, MP3, AC-3, MPEG-2 and similar) is refused with a sentence naming it. If you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job then offers to help (next section).
39	
40	### Files macOS cannot open, and ffmpeg
41	
42	When macOS refuses a file and `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` are both installed on this Mac, Frame Job asks before doing anything. It looks in your `PATH` first, then in `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/local/bin`, `/usr/bin` and `/bin`; to use one particular build, run `defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegPath /path/to/ffmpeg` (its `ffprobe` is taken from the same folder when one is there). The alert, "Frame Job cannot open *file*.", says what it would cost: a quick **Repackage** that copies the streams, or a **Convert** that re-encodes, with the size and the time it would take. Tick **Do this automatically from now on** to have your answer remembered: always, if you accept, or never, if you cancel. The converted file goes into the same Rewrapped folder, and the original is untouched. A conversion that fails shows "Could not convert *file* with ffmpeg: *reason*". Unlike a WebM copy, a conversion that is later deleted is not made again when the project opens: the media stays missing until you relink it. Frame Job does not ship ffmpeg; without one, this step never appears. To be asked again after ticking "Do this automatically", see [Settings](settings.md#limits).
43	
44	An agent's import never shows this question. Unless you have chosen "always", the file is refused instead.
45	
46	### Files that are refused
47	
48	- **A codec this Mac cannot decode** is refused at import with a sentence naming it, for example "*file* is AV1 video, which needs an M3 or later Mac." or "*file* is VP9 Profile 1 video, which this Mac cannot decode; VP9 Profiles 0 and 2 import." VP8 is refused the same way. A file in a codec this Mac does decode still imports even when some of its data is damaged.
49	- **A `.cube` the LUT reader cannot read** is refused naming the line and the problem, for example "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65."
50	- "Could not read *file*." means the file is damaged or not a format Frame Job reads.
51	- "*file* has no video or audio the app can open." means the file holds neither.
52	- "Timed out reading *file*." means the check took longer than 30 seconds, usually because the file is on a stalled network volume.
53	
54	## What a `.framejob` package holds
55	
56	A package is a folder that the Finder shows as one file:
57	
58	| Inside | What it is |
59	|---|---|
60	| `project.json` | The edit itself: canvas, media list, tracks, clips, markers. The only thing a package needs in order to open. |
61	| `cache/` | Things Frame Job can rebuild: filmstrip thumbnails, waveforms, the voice-detection and sync analyses, transcripts, reversed clips, speed-ramp audio, the shot changes, faces, sound events and subjects (people and salient regions) found for an agent, the faces and subjects drawn by View ▸ Show Subjects, and the person masks found for one or made for a clip with Remove Background (`cache/analysis/`; a minute of 1080p video's masks take about 62 MB). A package with a missing or damaged `cache/` still opens and just redraws. |
62	| `media/` | Only after **Consolidate Media…**: copies of the footage (see [Consolidate Media](#consolidate-media)). |
63	| `graphics/` | Only once you add a graphic: graphic modules, their fonts, images and kept versions. See [Graphics](graphics.md). |
64	
65	**Media is referenced, not copied.** By default a project remembers where each file lives (its path and a Finder bookmark, so a moved file is often found again) and reads it from there. The package stays small, but it depends on the footage staying put. Consolidate Media is how you make a package hold everything it needs.
66	
67	Caches are built in the background after an open, an import or a relink, and the timeline fills in as they finish. Frame Job builds at most two files' sound caches at a time, on threads of their own, so importing many long files at once does not hold up playback or a speed ramp's sound. A cache that already matches its file is never rebuilt. Moving, copying or consolidating the package keeps its caches. Until an untitled project is first saved, its caches live in a temporary folder; the first save copies them in.
68	
69	*Transcripts* cost money to rebuild when they came from the cloud engine, so treat `cache/transcripts/` as worth keeping. See [Captions](captions.md).
70	
71	## Missing media and Relink
72	
73	A project always opens, even when files it uses have moved or been deleted. Clips whose file is gone keep their place on the timeline and show a slate in their place, and their media rows wear the **missing** badge.
74	
75	When a project opens with files missing, Frame Job offers the **Missing media** sheet once: "The project opened without these files: their clips keep their place on the timeline and show a slate until the files are found." Each missing file is listed with its old path and a **Locate…** button.
76	
77	- Choosing a file for one entry also looks in that file's folder for the other missing files by name, and fills in each one it finds. A shoot moved as one folder is usually found with one Locate….
78	- A located row's button turns into **Change…**.
79	- The footnote counts the missing files ("3 files").
80	- **Relink** stays off until at least one file is located, then applies every choice as one undo step ("Relink Media"). You do not have to locate them all: the ones you skip stay missing, and you can relink them later from the Media tab. **Cancel** changes nothing.
81	- The sheet is offered once, when the window opens, and not over another sheet that is already showing.
82	
83	Relinking checks the new file as an import does. The media takes the new file's duration, size, frame rate and audio/video flags. A clip that runs past the end of a shorter new file is shortened to end with it. A file of another kind (a sound file for a video entry, say) is refused, and the reason is shown after the other relinks are applied. A WebM or MKV chosen as the new file is copied as on import.
84	
85	To relink one file at any time, use **Relink…** on its Media-tab row: "Choose the file for "*name*"."
86	
87	A consolidated package that has been moved or renamed finds its own copies again when it opens: any missing media whose file sits in the package's `media/` folder under the same name is pointed back at it, with no sheet. A screen recording's cursor file is found again the same way.
88	
89	*Agents:* `relink_media` (takes `media` and `path`; the app checks the new file itself). `get_project`'s `missing_media` lists what needs it.
90	
91	## Limits
92	
93	- Consolidate Media needs a saved project.
94	- Canvas width and height are even numbers from 16 to 16384 px.
95	- A project holds at most 4,096 clips and 64 tracks (counting those inside nests), 1,024 markers and 1,024 media files, with nests up to 8 deep.
96	- The Add Media… and Open panels list movies, M4A, MP3, WAV, AIFF, PNG, JPEG, HEIC and (Add Media… only) `.cube`. Other sound and picture formats import only by a drop on the Media tab, or through `import_media`.
97	- `.cube` files are imported, not opened: File ▸ Open… does not take one, and a `.cube` dropped on the window or the Dock is not imported. Use Add Media… or a drop on the Media tab.
98	- A project file that is damaged or out of range fails to open with a message naming the problem; the package is not rewritten. A package saved by a newer Frame Job reports "project format version *N* is newer than this build understands (version *M*); update Frame Job to open it". A package with no readable `project.json` reports "*name* does not contain a readable project.json."
