453	    /// AVFoundation's view of a movie or a sound file.
454	    private static func probeAsset(_ url: URL) async throws -> MediaDescriptor {
455	        let asset = AVURLAsset(url: url, options: [AVURLAssetPreferPreciseDurationAndTimingKey: true])
456	        guard let duration = try? await asset.load(.duration), duration.isNumeric else {
457	            throw ImportError.unreadable(url)
458	        }
459	        let videoTracks = (try? await asset.loadTracks(withMediaType: .video)) ?? []
460	        let audioTracks = (try? await asset.loadTracks(withMediaType: .audio)) ?? []
461	        guard !videoTracks.isEmpty || !audioTracks.isEmpty else {
462	            throw ImportError.noTracks(url)
463	        }
464	
465	        var width = 0
466	        var height = 0
467	        var fps = Fps.thirty
468	        var hasAlpha = false
469	        var color: MediaColor?
470	        if let track = videoTracks.first {
471	            let natural = (try? await track.load(.naturalSize)) ?? .zero
472	            let transform = (try? await track.load(.preferredTransform)) ?? .identity
473	            // `applying` maps the whole rectangle, so a 90° preferred
474	            // transform swaps the components and negates one of them; the
475	            // magnitudes are the display size.
476	            let mapped = natural.applying(transform)
477	            width = Int(abs(mapped.width).rounded())
478	            height = Int(abs(mapped.height).rounded())
479	            fps = await frameRate(of: track)
480	            let descriptions = (try? await track.load(.formatDescriptions)) ?? []
481	            hasAlpha = hasAlphaChannel(descriptions)
482	            color = detectedColor(descriptions) ?? detectedPQ(descriptions, track: track, asset: asset)
483	            // One frame through the decoder: `isPlayable` says yes to files
484	            // nothing here decodes (spec §11 #216).
485	            guard DecoderSupport.decodesFirstFrame(of: track, in: asset) else {
486	                throw ImportError.undecodable(url, sentence: DecoderSupport.refusal(
487	                    fileName: url.lastPathComponent, descriptions: descriptions))
488	            }
489	        }
490	
491	        let kind: MediaKind = videoTracks.isEmpty ? .audio : .video
492	        return MediaDescriptor(
493	            path: url.path, bookmark: bookmarkString(for: url), kind: kind,
494	            duration: CompositionBuilder.ticks(duration), width: width, height: height, fps: fps,
495	            hasVideo: !videoTracks.isEmpty, hasAudio: !audioTracks.isEmpty, hasAlpha: hasAlpha,
496	            color: color)
497	    }

499	    /// A track's rate as an exact rational. `nominalFrameRate` is a Float and
500	    /// lies slightly (29.97003 for 30000/1001), so it is matched against the
501	    /// common rates rather than trusted; a file that reports nothing falls
502	    /// back to `minFrameDuration`, which IS exact when the container carries
503	    /// it.
504	    private static func frameRate(of track: AVAssetTrack) async -> Fps {
505	        var nominal = Double((try? await track.load(.nominalFrameRate)) ?? 0)
506	        if !(nominal > 0), let minimum = try? await track.load(.minFrameDuration),
507	            minimum.isNumeric, minimum.seconds > 0 {
508	            nominal = 1 / minimum.seconds
509	        }
510	        return rationalFrameRate(nominal)
511	    }

---
title: "Import media"
description: "Bring movies, sound, pictures and LUTs into a project with Add Media… or a Finder drop, and find out why a file won't come in."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Importing puts a file in the project's Media tab, ready to place on the timeline. Frame Job reads the file from where it already is, so nothing is copied and the project stays small.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Add Media…"
  keys="⇧⌘I"
  where={['Media tab ▸ Add Media…', 'Drag from the Finder onto the Media tab']}
  tools={['import_media', 'add_media']}
/>

<Shot
  name="10b-media-tab.inspector"
  alt="The Media tab of the inspector, with the Add Media… button and its ⇧⌘I shortcut at the top of the list, and a count of the project's items beside them."
/>

## Add media

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Add Media…** (<kbd>⇧⌘I</kbd>), or **Add Media…** at the top of the Media tab.

2. Pick one or more files, and choose **Open**.

</Steps>

Frame Job checks every file, then adds the ones it can read to the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) together, as one undo step. The step is called **Add Media**, or **Add 3 Media Files** for three.

Adding a file that's already in the list changes nothing. A file Frame Job can't read shows an alert naming it, and the rest are still added.

## Drop on the Media tab

Drag files from the Finder onto the Media tab to add them to this project. It works like **Add Media…**, with one difference: a drop has no list of allowed types, so Frame Job tries every file you drop. That's how a format the panels don't list gets in.

## What each way takes

The **Add Media…** and **File ▸ Open…** panels only let you pick the types they list. To bring in anything else, drop it on the Media tab.

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Movies | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| PNG, JPEG and HEIC | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `.cube` LUTs | Yes | No | Yes |
| TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP | No | No | Yes |
| CAF, FLAC and other sound macOS plays | No | No | Yes |

| --- | --- |

- [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/)

---
title: "WebM and Matroska files"
description: "How Frame Job brings in .webm and .mkv files by copying their streams into a movie, what the copy can carry, and where the copies live."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

macOS won't open a WebM or MKV file directly, so Frame Job copies its video and sound into a QuickTime movie the first time you bring one in. Nothing is re-encoded, so no quality is lost, and your original stays where it is.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Add Media…', 'File ▸ Open…']}
  keys={['⇧⌘I', '⌘O']}
  where="Drag to the Media tab"
  tools={['import_media', 'open_project', 'relink_media']}
/>

## How a file is rewrapped

Add, open or relink the file as you would any other. There's no question to answer: the copy starts by itself, and the clip then plays from the copy.

Frame Job recognises these files by what's inside them, not by their name, so a Matroska file with the wrong extension still imports when you drop it on the Media tab.

| Stream | What the copy carries |
| --- | --- |
| Video | VP9, AV1, H.264 or HEVC |
| Sound | Opus, Vorbis or AAC |

Only the first video track and the first audio track are copied. Any other track, such as a second language or subtitles, stays behind in the original.

If the end of the file is damaged or cut short, the copy holds everything up to that point.

Some of these codecs can still be refused because this Mac can't decode them: VP8, AV1 on a Mac without a hardware decoder, and VP9 Profile 1 or 3. Nothing is copied, and the alert says why. See [Codecs this Mac can't decode](/projects/import-media/#codecs-this-mac-cant-decode).

## The name in the Media tab

The media keeps the original's name. Hover over its row in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) and the tooltip gives the original's path and says the file was copied into Frame Job's Rewrapped folder.

## The Copying Movie window

A copy that takes more than a second shows a small **Copying Movie** window, with a progress bar and how much has been copied, such as "412 MB of 1.2 GB". It reads "Reading the file…" until the copy starts.

Choose **Cancel** to stop. The copy stops, nothing is added, no alert appears and no partial file is left behind. If you were opening the file with **File ▸ Open…**, no project opens. If you were adding several files, the others carry on.

The window never takes the keyboard from a Frame Job window, so you can keep editing while it runs. Copies happen one at a time.

## Free space

Before copying, Frame Job checks that the disk has room. If it doesn't, nothing is copied and the alert says what's needed:

> Not enough free space to open *file*: its video and sound need about *size* on “*volume*”, which has *size* free. Nothing was copied.

If Frame Job can't read how much space the volume has, the copy goes ahead.

## The Rewrapped folder

Copies live in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Rewrapped/`, which all your projects share. Importing the same file again uses its copy instead of making another, even in a different project. If the original has changed, Frame Job makes a new copy.

Frame Job never deletes anything from this folder, so copies pile up. You can clear it yourself:

- WebM and MKV copies are made again the next time a project that uses them opens, as long as the original is still there.
- [ffmpeg conversions](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/#a-lost-conversion-stays-missing) live here too, and they aren't made again. Their media stays missing until you relink it.

[Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/) copies the movie, not the WebM, into the package. The row's tooltip then says it was copied into this project's package.

## Streams the copy can't carry

If a stream is in a codec the copy can't carry, the file is refused with a sentence naming it, for example:

> *file* has FLAC audio, which Frame Job cannot copy out of a WebM or Matroska file.

This applies to FLAC, MP3, MP2, AC-3, E-AC-3, DTS, TrueHD and PCM sound, Vorbis whose headers can't be read, and MPEG-2, MPEG-4 Part 2, Theora and ProRes video. A codec without a familiar name appears under its Matroska codec ID. A compressed or encrypted track is refused the same way: "*file* has a compressed or encrypted video track, which Frame Job cannot copy out of a WebM or Matroska file."

If you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job then offers to help. See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/). Without it, the sentence stands and the file stays out.

## Colour is kept

The copy keeps the colour the file states: HLG, HDR10 (PQ), or a BT.709, BT.601 or BT.2020 SDR picture. Frame Job reads it from the file's colour information or, for VP9, from the video itself. HDR10 metadata carries over.

A file that states no colour is shown as macOS reads it.

## If a copy goes missing

If a copy is deleted or moved to the Trash, the project makes it again from the original the next time it opens. The **Copying Movie** window shows as usual.

This needs the original to be in place and still be a WebM or Matroska file. If that copy is cancelled or fails, the file shows as missing, with a slate, the **missing** badge and **Relink…**, and the next open tries again.

## With an agent

An agent's import shows no window and waits for the copy to finish. `import_media` reports the copy as the file it added and names the file you asked for as the original. If the copy can't carry a stream, an agent doesn't get the ffmpeg question: see [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/#with-an-agent).

## Related

- [Import media](/projects/import-media/)
- [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/)
- [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/)
- [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/)

input.content:
---
title: "Convert files with ffmpeg"
description: "Use your own ffmpeg to bring in a file macOS can't open: what Frame Job asks, what it copies or re-encodes, and how to change your answer."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

When macOS can't open a file and you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job can use it to repackage or convert the file on import. Frame Job doesn't include ffmpeg, and without your own copy this step never appears.

<AtAGlance
  where={['The alert that appears on import ▸ Repackage or Convert']}
  tools={['import_media', 'relink_media']}
  needs="Your own ffmpeg and ffprobe, both installed on this Mac."
/>

## Repackage or convert a file

<Steps>

1. Add, open or relink the file as usual. If macOS can't open it, an alert appears: "Frame Job cannot open “*file*”."

2. Read what it would cost. The alert names the codecs and gives the size and the time.

3. Choose **Repackage** or **Convert** to go ahead, or **Cancel** to leave the file out.

</Steps>

The first button reads **Repackage** or **Convert** depending on the work to be done:

| The button | What the alert tells you |
| --- | --- |
| **Repackage** | Every stream can be copied as it is. No re-encoding, no loss of quality, and a few seconds' work. |
| **Convert** | The video can be copied, but the sound has to be re-encoded to AAC. That also takes a few seconds. |
| **Convert** | This Mac can't decode the video, so the whole file has to be re-encoded to H.264. The alert gives its picture size and length, and says it takes at least as long as the clip runs, usually longer. |

If you choose **Cancel**, Frame Job then shows the reason it couldn't read the file.

A conversion shows no progress window. The file appears when it's finished. If you add several files that need this step, Frame Job asks about them one at a time.

## What's copied and what's re-encoded

Each stream is copied when it can be, and re-encoded when it can't.

| Stream | Copied unchanged | Otherwise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Video | H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG, MPEG-4, QuickTime Animation and DV | Re-encoded to H.264 |
| Sound | AAC, ALAC and PCM | Re-encoded to 256 kbps AAC |

The H.264 encode uses x264 at CRF 18 when your ffmpeg has it. Without x264 it uses Apple's VideoToolbox encoder, at a bitrate worked out from the picture size and frame rate, from 2 to 60 Mbps. Either way the result is 8-bit 4:2:0, so a 10-bit source comes in as 8-bit.

VP9 Profile 0 or 2 with a known frame rate is copied too, with AAC or ALAC sound beside it, and any other sound is re-encoded to AAC. Frame Job then checks that every frame of the copy sits exactly on the frame rate. If the copy fails that check, or won't open, it's re-encoded to H.264 once. Unless you've told Frame Job to do this automatically, it asks you again first.

Only the first video stream and the first audio stream are carried over. Subtitles and data streams are dropped. An attached cover image doesn't count as the picture, so a sound file with cover art comes in as sound.

## Where the converted file goes

The converted file goes into `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Rewrapped/`, the same folder as [WebM and MKV copies](/projects/webm-and-matroska/#the-rewrapped-folder). It keeps its own name in the Media tab, and your original is untouched.

Importing the same file again uses the finished conversion with no question, even if you've since removed ffmpeg or chosen never to convert. If the original's path, size or modification date has changed, it counts as a new file.

## Remember your answer

Tick **Do this automatically from now on** in the alert to keep the answer you give:

- Ticked with **Repackage** or **Convert**, such files are converted from then on without asking.
- Ticked with **Cancel**, they're never converted, and the import fails with its usual message.

There's no button to forget the answer. To be asked again, run this in Terminal while Frame Job is closed:

```sh
defaults delete com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegImport
```

That setting holds `ask`, `always` or `never`, and `ask` is the default.

## Finding ffmpeg

Frame Job needs both `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe`. With only one of them, this step doesn't appear.

It looks on your `PATH` first, then in `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/local/bin`, `/usr/bin` and `/bin`. It looks once per launch, so quit and reopen Frame Job after installing ffmpeg.

To use one particular build, name it in Terminal:

```sh
defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegPath /path/to/ffmpeg
```

`ffprobe` is then taken from beside it, or else found by the same search. If nothing runnable is at that path, Frame Job doesn't look anywhere else for `ffmpeg`, and this step doesn't appear.

## When a conversion fails

| The alert says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Could not convert *file* with ffmpeg: *reason*" | ffmpeg stopped with an error. The reason is its own last line, and without one the sentence ends at "ffmpeg." |
| "ffmpeg gave up converting *file*." | It ran out of time. |

A copy gets five minutes or twice the file's length, whichever is longer. A re-encode gets 30 minutes or 30 times the file's length. Neither gets more than 4 hours.

No partial file is left behind. If a conversion finishes but macOS still can't open the result, Frame Job throws it away and shows the original error, so the next import starts afresh.

## A lost conversion stays missing

Unlike a [WebM copy](/projects/webm-and-matroska/#if-a-copy-goes-missing), a conversion that's deleted isn't made again when the project opens. The media stays missing until you [relink it](/projects/relink-media/). Relinking to the original file goes through this step again.

## Files ffmpeg isn't offered for

Frame Job doesn't offer ffmpeg for:

- A picture or a `.cube` file it can't read.
- A file that timed out, because ffmpeg would stall on the same volume.
- A codec this Mac can't decode inside a file macOS can open, or inside a WebM or MKV file. See [Codecs this Mac can't decode](/projects/import-media/#codecs-this-mac-cant-decode).
- A WebM or MKV file refused for lack of [free space](/projects/webm-and-matroska/#free-space).
- A file in which ffprobe finds no video or audio.

## With an agent

An agent's import never shows this question. Unless you've chosen to convert automatically, the offer counts as declined and the file is refused with the reason, which also says how to get past it: import the file from the app's window, or set the answer to `always`.

With `always` set, `import_media` and `relink_media` convert without asking, and the import can take as long as the conversion does. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).

## Related

- [Import media](/projects/import-media/)
- [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/)
- [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/)

title: "Convert files with ffmpeg"
description: "Use your own ffmpeg to bring in a file macOS can't open: what Frame Job asks, what it copies or re-encodes, and how to change your answer."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

When macOS can't open a file and you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job can use it to repackage or convert the file on import. Frame Job doesn't include ffmpeg, and without your own copy this step never appears.

<AtAGlance
  where={['The alert that appears on import ▸ Repackage or Convert']}
  tools={['import_media', 'relink_media']}
  needs="Your own ffmpeg and ffprobe, both installed on this Mac."
/>

## Repackage or convert a file

<Steps>

1. Add, open or relink the file as usual. If macOS can't open it, an alert appears: "Frame Job cannot open “*file*”."

2. Read what it would cost. The alert names the codecs and gives the size and the time.

3. Choose **Repackage** or **Convert** to go ahead, or **Cancel** to leave the file out.

</Steps>

The first button reads **Repackage** or **Convert** depending on the work to be done:

| The button | What the alert tells you |
| --- | --- |
| **Repackage** | Every stream can be copied as it is. No re-encoding, no loss of quality, and a few seconds' work. |
| **Convert** | The video can be copied, but the sound has to be re-encoded to AAC. That also takes a few seconds. |
| **Convert** | This Mac can't decode the video, so the whole file has to be re-encoded to H.264. The alert gives its picture size and length, and says it takes at least as long as the clip runs, usually longer. |

If you choose **Cancel**, Frame Job then shows the reason it couldn't read the file.

A conversion shows no progress window. The file appears when it's finished. If you add several files that need this step, Frame Job asks about them one at a time.

## What's copied and what's re-encoded

Each stream is copied when it can be, and re-encoded when it can't.

| Stream | Copied unchanged | Otherwise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Video | H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG, MPEG-4, QuickTime Animation and DV | Re-encoded to H.264 |
| Sound | AAC, ALAC and PCM | Re-encoded to 256 kbps AAC |

The H.264 encode uses x264 at CRF 18 when your ffmpeg has it. Without x264 it uses Apple's VideoToolbox encoder, at a bitrate worked out from the picture size and frame rate, from 2 to 60 Mbps. Either way the result is 8-bit 4:2:0, so a 10-bit source comes in as 8-bit.

VP9 Profile 0 or 2 with a known frame rate is copied too, with AAC or ALAC sound beside it, and any other sound is re-encoded to AAC. - Ticked with **Repackage** or **Convert**, such files are converted from then on without asking.
- Ticked with **Cancel**, they're never converted, and the import fails with its usual message.

```sh
defaults delete com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegImport
```

```sh
defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegPath /path/to/ffmpeg
```

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

---
title: "Import media"
description: "Bring movies, sound, pictures and LUTs into a project with Add Media… or a Finder drop, and find out why a file won't come in."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

Importing puts a file in the project's Media tab, ready to place on the timeline. Frame Job reads the file from where it already is, so nothing is copied and the project stays small.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Add Media…"
  keys="⇧⌘I"
  where={['Media tab ▸ Add Media…', 'Drag from the Finder onto the Media tab']}
  tools={['import_media', 'add_media']}
/>

<Shot
  name="10b-media-tab.inspector"
  alt="The Media tab of the inspector, with the Add Media… button and its ⇧⌘I shortcut at the top of the list, and a count of the project's items beside them."
/>

## Add media

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Add Media…** (<kbd>⇧⌘I</kbd>), or **Add Media…** at the top of the Media tab.

2. Pick one or more files, and choose **Open**.

</Steps>

Frame Job checks every file, then adds the ones it can read to the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) together, as one undo step. The step is called **Add Media**, or **Add 3 Media Files** for three.

The files are in the Media tab, not on the timeline. Place them from there. Thumbnails and waveforms are built in the background, so they fill in a moment later.

Adding a file that's already in the list changes nothing. A file Frame Job can't read shows an alert naming it, and the rest are still added.

## Drop on the Media tab

Drag files from the Finder onto the Media tab to add them to this project. It works like **Add Media…**, with one difference: a drop has no list of allowed types, so Frame Job tries every file you drop. That's how a format the panels don't list gets in.

A Finder drop anywhere else on the window, such as the canvas or the timeline, doesn't add to this project. It opens the file as a new project of its own, as a drop on the Dock icon does. See [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/).

## What each way takes

The **Add Media…** and **File ▸ Open…** panels only let you pick the types they list. To bring in anything else, drop it on the Media tab.

| Files | **Add Media…** | **File ▸ Open…**, or a drop on the window or the Dock | A drop on the Media tab |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Movies | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| M4A, MP3, WAV and AIFF | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| PNG, JPEG and HEIC | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| `.cube` LUTs | Yes | No | Yes |
| TIFF, GIF, BMP, HEIF and WebP | No | No | Yes |
| CAF, FLAC and other sound macOS plays | No | No | Yes |

A `.cube` is imported, never opened. It sits in the Media tab and you apply it to clips as a [look](/color/luts/), or to a file as its [camera log](/hdr/log-luts/). It never goes on the timeline.

Caption files aren't media. Bring an `.srt` in with [Import Captions](/captions/import-captions/). Every format and codec Frame Job reads is listed in [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/).

## Referenced, not copied

A project remembers each file's path and a Finder bookmark, and reads the file from there. The package stays small, but it depends on your footage staying put. If you move a file, the bookmark often finds it again.

When you want a package that holds everything it needs, use [Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/).

WebM and Matroska files, and anything converted with ffmpeg, are the exception: Frame Job reads those from a copy it keeps in its own folder. See [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/) and [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).

## A project always opens

A project opens even when files it uses have moved or been deleted. Clips whose file is gone keep their place on the timeline and show a slate, and their rows in the Media tab wear the **missing** badge.

Those clips still export, showing the slate and with no sound. To bring them back, see [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/).

## Codecs this Mac can't decode

Before it adds a video, Frame Job decodes its first frame. If nothing on this Mac can decode it, the file is left out and an alert names the codec.

| The alert says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "*file* is VP8 video, which this Mac cannot decode." | VP8 doesn't import. |
| "*file* is AV1 video, which needs an M3 or later Mac." | AV1 needs a hardware decoder, which this Mac doesn't have. |
| "*file* is VP9 Profile 1 video, which this Mac cannot decode; VP9 Profiles 0 and 2 import." | VP9 Profiles 1 and 3 don't import. Profiles 0 and 2 do. |

Any other codec gets the same sentence with its own name. There's no way past these, and [ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/) isn't offered.

A file in a codec this Mac does decode still imports when some of its data is damaged.

## Import errors

| The alert says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Could not read *file*." | The file is damaged, or it isn't a format Frame Job reads. |
| "*file* has no video or audio the app can open." | The file holds neither. |
| "Timed out reading *file*." | The check took more than 30 seconds, usually because the file is on a stalled network volume. |
| "“Film.cube” is not a LUT Frame Job reads: line 2: LUT_3D_SIZE 200 is outside 2–65." | The `.cube` can't be read. The alert names the line and the problem. |

If you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job may offer to convert a file before it shows the first two of these. See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/).

## Good to know

- A project holds at most 1,024 media files.
- Undoing an import takes the files out of the project and leaves them on disk.

## With an agent

`import_media` does what **Add Media…** does, one file at a time, and it never stops to ask a question. `add_media` is different: it adds an entry from a description you supply and doesn't look at the file. Use it only to replay a project's own JSON. See [Tools: media](/mcp/tools-media/).

## Related

- [The Media tab](/projects/media-tab/)
- [Open a project](/projects/open-a-project/)
- [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/)
- [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/)

---
title: "WebM and Matroska files"
description: "How Frame Job brings in .webm and .mkv files by copying their streams into a movie, what the copy can carry, and where the copies live."
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

macOS won't open a WebM or MKV file directly, so Frame Job copies its video and sound into a QuickTime movie the first time you bring one in. Nothing is re-encoded, so no quality is lost, and your original stays where it is.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Add Media…', 'File ▸ Open…']}
  keys={['⇧⌘I', '⌘O']}
  where="Drag to the Media tab"
  tools={['import_media', 'open_project', 'relink_media']}
/>

## How a file is rewrapped

Add, open or relink the file as you would any other. There's no question to answer: the copy starts by itself, and the clip then plays from the copy.

Frame Job recognises these files by what's inside them, not by their name, so a Matroska file with the wrong extension still imports when you drop it on the Media tab.

| Stream | What the copy carries |
| --- | --- |
| Video | VP9, AV1, H.264 or HEVC |
| Sound | Opus, Vorbis or AAC |

Only the first video track and the first audio track are copied. Any other track, such as a second language or subtitles, stays behind in the original.

If the end of the file is damaged or cut short, the copy holds everything up to that point.

Some of these codecs can still be refused because this Mac can't decode them: VP8, AV1 on a Mac without a hardware decoder, and VP9 Profile 1 or 3. Nothing is copied, and the alert says why. See [Codecs this Mac can't decode](/projects/import-media/#codecs-this-mac-cant-decode).

## The name in the Media tab

The media keeps the original's name. Hover over its row in the [Media tab](/projects/media-tab/) and the tooltip gives the original's path and says the file was copied into Frame Job's Rewrapped folder.

## The Copying Movie window

A copy that takes more than a second shows a small **Copying Movie** window, with a progress bar and how much has been copied, such as "412 MB of 1.2 GB". It reads "Reading the file…" until the copy starts.

Choose **Cancel** to stop. The copy stops, nothing is added, no alert appears and no partial file is left behind. If you were opening the file with **File ▸ Open…**, no project opens. If you were adding several files, the others carry on.

The window never takes the keyboard from a Frame Job window, so you can keep editing while it runs. Copies happen one at a time.

## Free space

Before copying, Frame Job checks that the disk has room. If it doesn't, nothing is copied and the alert says what's needed:

> Not enough free space to open *file*: its video and sound need about *size* on “*volume*”, which has *size* free. Nothing was copied.

If Frame Job can't read how much space the volume has, the copy goes ahead.

## The Rewrapped folder

Copies live in `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Rewrapped/`, which all your projects share. Importing the same file again uses its copy instead of making another, even in a different project. If the original has changed, Frame Job makes a new copy.

Frame Job never deletes anything from this folder, so copies pile up. You can clear it yourself:

- WebM and MKV copies are made again the next time a project that uses them opens, as long as the original is still there.
- [ffmpeg conversions](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/#a-lost-conversion-stays-missing) live here too, and they aren't made again. Their media stays missing until you relink it.

[Consolidate Media](/projects/consolidate-media/) copies the movie, not the WebM, into the package. The row's tooltip then says it was copied into this project's package.

## Streams the copy can't carry

If a stream is in a codec the copy can't carry, the file is refused with a sentence naming it, for example:

> *file* has FLAC audio, which Frame Job cannot copy out of a WebM or Matroska file.

This applies to FLAC, MP3, MP2, AC-3, E-AC-3, DTS, TrueHD and PCM sound, Vorbis whose headers can't be read, and MPEG-2, MPEG-4 Part 2, Theora and ProRes video. A codec without a familiar name appears under its Matroska codec ID. A compressed or encrypted track is refused the same way: "*file* has a compressed or encrypted video track, which Frame Job cannot copy out of a WebM or Matroska file."

If you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job then offers to help. See [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/). Without it, the sentence stands and the file stays out.

## Colour is kept

The copy keeps the colour the file states: HLG, HDR10 (PQ), or a BT.709, BT.601 or BT.2020 SDR picture. Frame Job reads it from the file's colour information or, for VP9, from the video itself. HDR10 metadata carries over.

A file that states no colour is shown as macOS reads it.

## If a copy goes missing

If a copy is deleted or moved to the Trash, the project makes it again from the original the next time it opens. The **Copying Movie** window shows as usual.

This needs the original to be in place and still be a WebM or Matroska file. If that copy is cancelled or fails, the file shows as missing, with a slate, the **missing** badge and **Relink…**, and the next open tries again.

## With an agent

An agent's import shows no window and waits for the copy to finish. `import_media` reports the copy as the file it added and names the file you asked for as the original. If the copy can't carry a stream, an agent doesn't get the ffmpeg question: see [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/#with-an-agent).

## Related

- [Import media](/projects/import-media/)
- [Convert files with ffmpeg](/projects/ffmpeg-conversion/)
- [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/)
- [Relink missing media](/projects/relink-media/)

---
title: "Convert files with ffmpeg"
description: "Use your own ffmpeg to bring in a file macOS can't open: what Frame Job asks, what it copies or re-encodes, and how to change your answer."
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

When macOS can't open a file and you have ffmpeg installed, Frame Job can use it to repackage or convert the file on import. Frame Job doesn't include ffmpeg, and without your own copy this step never appears.

<AtAGlance
  where={['The alert that appears on import ▸ Repackage or Convert']}
  tools={['import_media', 'relink_media']}
  needs="Your own ffmpeg and ffprobe, both installed on this Mac."
/>

## Repackage or convert a file

<Steps>

1. Add, open or relink the file as usual. If macOS can't open it, an alert appears: "Frame Job cannot open “*file*”."

2. Read what it would cost. The alert names the codecs and gives the size and the time.

3. Choose **Repackage** or **Convert** to go ahead, or **Cancel** to leave the file out.

</Steps>

The first button reads **Repackage** or **Convert** depending on the work to be done:

| The button | What the alert tells you |
| --- | --- |
| **Repackage** | Every stream can be copied as it is. No re-encoding, no loss of quality, and a few seconds' work. |
| **Convert** | The video can be copied, but the sound has to be re-encoded to AAC. That also takes a few seconds. |
| **Convert** | This Mac can't decode the video, so the whole file has to be re-encoded to H.264. The alert gives its picture size and length, and says it takes at least as long as the clip runs, usually longer. |

If you choose **Cancel**, Frame Job then shows the reason it couldn't read the file.

A conversion shows no progress window. The file appears when it's finished. If you add several files that need this step, Frame Job asks about them one at a time.

## What's copied and what's re-encoded

Each stream is copied when it can be, and re-encoded when it can't.

| Stream | Copied unchanged | Otherwise |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Video | H.264, HEVC, ProRes, MJPEG, MPEG-4, QuickTime Animation and DV | Re-encoded to H.264 |
| Sound | AAC, ALAC and PCM | Re-encoded to 256 kbps AAC |

The H.264 encode uses x264 at CRF 18 when your ffmpeg has it. Without x264 it uses Apple's VideoToolbox encoder, at a bitrate worked out from the picture size and frame rate, from 2 to 60 Mbps. Either way the result is 8-bit 4:2:0, so a 10-bit source comes in as 8-bit.

VP9 Profile 0 or 2 with a known frame rate is copied too, with AAC or ALAC sound beside it, and any other sound is re-encoded to AAC. Frame Job then checks that every frame of the copy sits exactly on the frame rate. If the copy fails that check, or won't open, it's re-encoded to H.264 once. Unless you've told Frame Job to do this automatically, it asks you again first.

Only the first video stream and the first audio stream are carried over. Subtitles and data streams are dropped. An attached cover image doesn't count as the picture, so a sound file with cover art comes in as sound.

## Where the converted file goes

The converted file goes into `~/Library/Application Support/Frame Job/Rewrapped/`, the same folder as [WebM and MKV copies](/projects/webm-and-matroska/#the-rewrapped-folder). It keeps its own name in the Media tab, and your original is untouched.

Importing the same file again uses the finished conversion with no question, even if you've since removed ffmpeg or chosen never to convert. If the original's path, size or modification date has changed, it counts as a new file.

## Remember your answer

Tick **Do this automatically from now on** in the alert to keep the answer you give:

- Ticked with **Repackage** or **Convert**, such files are converted from then on without asking.
- Ticked with **Cancel**, they're never converted, and the import fails with its usual message.

There's no button to forget the answer. To be asked again, run this in Terminal while Frame Job is closed:

```sh
defaults delete com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegImport
```

That setting holds `ask`, `always` or `never`, and `ask` is the default.

## Finding ffmpeg

Frame Job needs both `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe`. With only one of them, this step doesn't appear.

It looks on your `PATH` first, then in `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `/opt/local/bin`, `/usr/bin` and `/bin`. It looks once per launch, so quit and reopen Frame Job after installing ffmpeg.

To use one particular build, name it in Terminal:

```sh
defaults write com.kgalligan.FrameJob RCFFmpegPath /path/to/ffmpeg
```

`ffprobe` is then taken from beside it, or else found by the same search. If nothing runnable is at that path, Frame Job doesn't look anywhere else for `ffmpeg`, and this step doesn't appear.

## When a conversion fails

| The alert says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Could not convert *file* with ffmpeg: *reason*" | ffmpeg stopped with an error. The reason is its own last line, and without one the sentence ends at "ffmpeg." |
| "ffmpeg gave up converting *file*." | It ran out of time. |

A copy gets five minutes or twice the file's length, whichever is longer. A re-encode gets 30 minutes or 30 times the file's length. Neither gets more than 4 hours.

No partial file is left behind. If a conversion finishes but macOS still can't open the result, Frame Job throws it away and shows the original error, so the next import starts afresh.

## A lost conversion stays missing

Unlike a [WebM copy](/projects/webm-and-matroska/#if-a-copy-goes-missing), a conversion that's deleted isn't made again when the project opens. The media stays missing until you [relink it](/projects/relink-media/). Relinking to the original file goes through this step again.

## Files ffmpeg isn't offered for

Frame Job doesn't offer ffmpeg for:

- A picture or a `.cube` file it can't read.
- A file that timed out, because ffmpeg would stall on the same volume.
- A codec this Mac can't decode inside a file macOS can open, or inside a WebM or MKV file. See [Codecs this Mac can't decode](/projects/import-media/#codecs-this-mac-cant-decode).
- A WebM or MKV file refused for lack of [free space](/projects/webm-and-matroska/#free-space).
- A file in which ffprobe finds no video or audio.

## With an agent

An agent's import never shows this question. Unless you've chosen to convert automatically, the offer counts as declined and the file is refused with the reason, which also says how to get past it: import the file from the app's window, or set the answer to `always`.

With `always` set, `import_media` and `relink_media` convert without asking, and the import can take as long as the conversion does. See [How tool calls behave](/mcp/tool-calls/).

## Related

- [Import media](/projects/import-media/)
- [WebM and Matroska files](/projects/webm-and-matroska/)
- [Supported file formats](/reference/file-formats/)

<system-reminder>
Contents of /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/help-docs/docs/site/CLAUDE.md:

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>
